BREAKING: The US goods trade deficit widened by -$2.8 billion in September, or -2.1%, to -$134.9 billion, its widest gap since March 2025.

Imports rose +$8.1 billion, or +2.4%, to a record $344.2 billion.

This jump was led by a +7.5% MoM increase in capital goods, which include computers and accessories, semiconductors, and telecommunications equipment fueling the AI buildout.

Now, the capital goods deficit has widened by -$54.3 billion YoY, accounting for more than the entire increase in the overall trade deficit.

Meanwhile, US goods exports jumped +$5.3 billion in September, or +2.6%, to $209.2 billion, driven by a +12.8% increase in food shipments.

The US trade deficit is rapidly widening again.

Generally speaking, for this chart:
Positive delta: net short puts or net long calls.
Negative delta: net long puts or net short calls.

Positive gamma: net long options.
Negative gamma: net short options.

Positive vega: net long options, weighted toward near-the-money and longer-dated.
Negative vega: net short options, same weighting. Not a wings read.

AI is burning Big Tech's free cash flow:

The combined CapEx of Amazon, $AMZN, Alphabet, $GOOGL, Meta, $META, and Microsoft, $MSFT, rose +$36.9 billion in Q3 2026, to a record $201.9 billion.

This figure has more than doubled over the last 12 months and is up +356% since Q1 2024.

Big Tech has now spent $1.6 trillion on CapEx over the last 3 years.

Meanwhile, the combined free cash flow of these companies fell -$33.1 billion last quarter, to -$26.4 billion, its lowest on record.

Free cash flow among these firms has dropped -$88.2 billion over the last year.

Only Microsoft reported positive free cash flow in Q3.

Looking ahead, these 4 companies plan to spend another $232 billion on CapEx in Q4, potentially lifting their combined CapEx to a record $740 billion in 2026.

Big Tech is undertaking one of the largest infrastructure buildouts in history.
